questions.question: If you cannot tell if the road is icy and slippery, what should you do?

options.text: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icy but are not sure, open your window and feel the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on these items, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: It should only be done in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops cargo from sliding.
questions.explanation: Blocking keeps cargo from moving while the vehicle is traveling.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Slowly build up over several minutes.
Reach a normal level within a few seconds.
Start high, then drop quickly while the engine runs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach a normal level within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level in seconds. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after it starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that have not washed away.
Gravel washes into the middle of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that have not washed away.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil drippings that have not yet washed away, making a slippery surface.

questions.question: When you see a green light at a drawbridge, can you cross?

options.text: Yes, you can cross without stopping.
No, you must wait for the light to turn yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you can cross without stopping.
questions.explanation: You do not need to stop before crossing a drawbridge with a green light. However, slow down and make sure it is safe before crossing.

questions.question: How often must drivers check that cargo is secure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: After cargo is secured on a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check the cargo again.
You should not let others inspect the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the cargo every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, what might be required?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require the engine to be running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Where should carry-on baggage be stored on a bus?

options.text: In the aisle for easy access.

questions.correctAnswerText: Away from the aisle.
questions.explanation: Baggage must never be left in the aisle or doorway. All luggage must be positioned so riders can exit through any window or door in an emergency.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, what will likely happen to your vehicle's speed?
questions.correctAnswerText: It will increase.
questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to speed up on a downhill slope. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressed down gradually.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly and steadily. This helps your vehicle stop smoothly and safely.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: A basic vehicle control skills test may include parallel parking, straight line backing, and other parking maneuvers.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Should be expected to be on the roadway.
Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. A cardboard box might look harmless but could contain something heavy or hard that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: Dual tires should:

options.text: Always come into contact with one another.
Come into contact with one another fairly regularly.
Not come into contact with one another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not come into contact with one another.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.correctAnswerText: About one-third.
questions.explanation: Wet roads have less traction. Reduce your speed by about one-third when driving on wet pavement.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space between you and the vehicle ahead. This makes it easier for the tailgater to pass. Speeding up is not safe because the driver may continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: If turning to avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should not brake as it may cause the wheels to lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not brake as it may cause the wheels to lock.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking can cause your wheels to lock and make your vehicle skid out of control.

questions.question: When checking power steering hoses during a pre-trip inspection, you should look for:

options.text: Extra hose pieces available for repairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look specifically for leaks.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold down the pedal for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake pedal returns to its normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold down the pedal for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then push it down hard and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake system problem.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an indication of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads free of oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: Signs of brake damage include cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn dangerously thin. Clean pads are a sign of healthy brakes.
